1	"""Deterministic 2D grid A* planner.
2	
3	Public entry points: ``plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None,
4	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
5	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False)``, ``plan_any(width, height, blocked,
6	start, goals, costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None,
7	max_expanded=None, snapshot=False, max_cost=None, allow_wait=False)``,
8	``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
9	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None,
10	allow_wait=False)``,
11	``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None, trace=False,
12	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
13	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False)``,
14	``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
15	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
16	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False)``,
17	``replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None,
18	dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False, allow_wait=False)``,
19	``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)``,
20	``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None, trace=False)``
21	and
22	``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
23	trace=False)``.
24	
25	Semantics:
26	- Four-neighborhood moves, Manhattan heuristic. Without ``costs`` each step
27	  has unit cost. With ``costs`` (a height-by-width matrix of positive
28	  integers, row-major: ``costs[y][x]``) entering a cell costs that cell's
29	  value; the start cell's cost is never counted, so ``cost`` is the sum of
30	  the costs of the cells entered along the path.
31	- Tie-breaking is fully specified and order-independent: compare f, then h,
32	  then the (x, y) coordinate in lexicographic order.
33	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the nodes popped from the priority queue and
34	  closed for the first time (the goal counts when reached; stale heap
35	  entries and duplicate closings do not).
36	- Returns ``{"path": [...], "cost": int, "expanded": int}`` on success and
37	  ``{"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": int}`` when unreachable.
38	- When ``trace`` is true, both kinds of results additionally include
39	  ``expanded_nodes``: the list of coordinate tuples closed for the first
40	  time, in expansion order (includes the start, and the goal on success);
41	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. The field is omitted entirely when
42	  ``trace`` is false or omitted.
43	
44	Search budget (``max_expanded``):
45	- ``max_expanded`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key,
46	  value, exception type and validation order of the default behavior
47	  untouched. Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a
48	  bool: other types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise
49	  ``ValueError``. These checks run after all existing grid, costs,
50	  ``trace`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` validation (including the frame-0
51	  check) and before the search starts.
52	- The budget counts closed nodes (exactly what ``expanded`` counts); once
53	  the limit is reached no further node is closed. When the budget is
54	  provided the result always carries an additional ``status`` field:
55	  ``"found"`` when the goal was closed within the limit (the usual
56	  ``path``/``cost`` are returned), ``"unreachable"`` when the candidates
57	  were exhausted without reaching the goal, and ``"budget_exhausted"``
58	  when live candidates remained but the budget stopped the search (then
59	  ``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded`` is the actual closed
60	  count, at most ``max_expanded``).
61	- The budget applies identically in static and dynamic mode and never
62	  changes expansion order, path choice, trace entries or determinism: a
63	  budgeted trace is a prefix of the unbudgeted one. With ``trace=True``
64	  only actually closed nodes are recorded, so a zero budget records
65	  nothing -- even when ``start == goal`` a zero budget returns
66	  ``budget_exhausted`` with ``expanded == 0``; the single-point success
67	  result requires at least one closed node (``max_expanded >= 1``).
68	- ``replay`` is unaffected: it keeps validating candidate paths only and
69	  accepts no budget parameter.
70	
71	Cost limit (``max_cost``):
72	- ``max_cost`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key, value,
73	  exception type and validation order of the previous behavior untouched.
74	  Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a bool: other
75	  types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise ``ValueError``. The
76	  check runs after all existing grid, costs, ``trace``, ``dynamic_blocked``,
77	  ``max_expanded`` and ``snapshot`` validation and before the search
78	  starts.
79	- The limit caps the accumulated entering-cell cost of a route, measured
80	  from the start (the start cell still costs 0 and each entered cell costs
81	  its ``costs`` value, or 1 without ``costs``). A candidate whose
82	  accumulated cost would exceed the limit is discarded; a candidate at
83	  exactly the limit still competes. The limit applies identically in
84	  static mode, dynamic mode and ``plan_any``, and never changes expansion
85	  order, tie-breaks, the minimum-cost choice, the multi-goal endpoint
86	  comparison or trace entries.
87	- When ``max_cost`` is provided the result always carries ``status``:
88	  ``"found"`` on success, and on failure ``"cost_exhausted"`` when at
89	  least one candidate was discarded for exceeding the limit, otherwise
90	  ``"unreachable"`` (``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded``
91	  counts the actually closed nodes). When ``max_expanded`` is also given,
92	  a budget stop still takes priority with ``"budget_exhausted"``.
93	  ``trace`` keeps recording only actually closed nodes, and the
94	  ``start == goal`` single-point zero-cost result and the zero-budget
95	  rules are unchanged.
96	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records the ``max_cost`` value
97	  when one was provided (and no new field when it was not). ``resume``
98	  treats a checkpoint without the field as ``None``, validates a present
99	  field with the same rules (``TypeError`` for wrong types, ``ValueError``
100	  for negative values or a state inconsistent with the limit) before any
101	  searching, and a resumed search is equivalent to one uninterrupted call
102	  with the same limit. ``replay`` accepts no ``max_cost`` parameter.
103	
104	Waiting in place (``allow_wait``):
105	- ``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``, ``plan_multi_start``, ``plan_k``
106	  and ``replay`` accept a final optional boolean ``allow_wait`` that
107	  defaults to ``False``. ``False`` -- or an omitted, ``None`` or empty
108	  ``dynamic_blocked`` -- keeps every key, value, exception type,
109	  validation order, four-neighborhood move, no-repeated-coordinate rule
110	  and tie-break of the previous behavior untouched. A non-bool
111	  ``allow_wait`` raises ``TypeError`` after the ``dynamic_blocked``
112	  checks (the frame-0 check included) and before the budget and snapshot
113	  checks; every other exception type and order is unchanged.
114	- With ``allow_wait=True`` a route may stay in its current cell from
115	  time ``t`` to time ``t + 1`` provided the cell is not blocked at frame
116	  ``t + 1``. Waiting adds no entering-cell cost (``cost`` still sums
117	  only the cells entered by moves, and ``max_cost`` caps only those) and
118	  is only generated while ``t + 1`` lies within the provided frames:
119	  after the last frame the last frame is still reused for moves but no
120	  further waits are generated. Consecutive waits repeat the same
121	  coordinate in the path; once a cell is left it may never be
122	  re-entered. ``start == goal`` still yields only the single-point
123	  zero-cost route.
124	- The minimum-cost choice, the endpoint selection and the complete-path
125	  lexicographic tie-break follow the existing rules, with the priority
126	  still f, then h, then the coordinate, then the time and finally the
127	  complete path, so results never depend on obstacle-set or in-frame
128	  iteration order. Wait states count toward ``expanded`` one per closing
129	  and the trace records their ``(x, y, t)`` triples; ``max_expanded``
130	  truncates them like any other state and the ``status`` values and
131	  priorities are unchanged. ``plan_k``, ``plan_batch``, multi-goal and
132	  multi-start results follow the same waiting semantics, and a
133	  successful path verifies in ``replay`` with the same cost and step
134	  count, the waits included in ``steps``.
135	- ``replay`` with ``allow_wait=True`` accepts consecutive stays only
136	  within the provided dynamic frames; stays in static mode or without
137	  frames, stays after the final frame and non-consecutive revisits all
138	  return the usual invalid structure. With ``diagnose=True`` a stay
139	  after the final frame reports the dedicated error
140	  ``wait_after_final_frame``.
141	- A budget-exhausted checkpoint records ``allow_wait`` when it was true
142	  and ``resume`` of such a checkpoint is equivalent to one uninterrupted
143	  call with the same setting. Checkpoints written without the field
144	  restore it as ``False``; a present non-bool field raises ``TypeError``
145	  and a field inconsistent with the recorded internal state raises
146	  ``ValueError``.
147	
148	Dynamic obstacles (``dynamic_blocked``):
149	- ``dynamic_blocked`` may be omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence, which
150	  leaves the static behavior above untouched. Otherwise it must be a
151	  sequence of frames; each frame is an iterable of grid coordinates that
152	  are blocked at that time frame. Frame 0 constrains ``start``; the
153	  coordinate at path index ``t`` must avoid both the static obstacles and
154	  frame ``t``, and frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame.
155	- Moves are still four-neighborhood only: no waiting in place and no
156	  repeated coordinates along the path. Because feasibility of a route
157	  depends on the coordinates it already visited, candidates that reach the
158	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
159	  states and are never merged: every route that satisfies the constraints
160	  can be explored. ``cost`` is still the sum of the costs of the cells
161	  entered; the start cell is never counted.
162	- The minimum-cost feasible route is returned. When total costs tie, the
163	  fixed priority is f, then h, then x, y, t, and candidates still tied are
164	  ordered lexicographically by their complete coordinate sequence, so the
165	  result never depends on the iteration order of the obstacle sets, the
166	  coordinates inside a frame, or the traversal order.
167	- In dynamic mode ``expanded_nodes`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples in
168	  actual closing order and ``expanded`` counts closed space-time route
169	  states one per entry; a discarded candidate is never recorded. When the
170	  same ``(x, y, t)`` is closed through different histories, its triple
171	  appears once per closing in closing order, and ``expanded`` counts each
172	  such entry. On failure ``path``/``cost`` are ``None``.
173	- Validation: the outer value must be a sequence and every frame an
174	  iterable of coordinates; strings/bytes and non-two-integer coordinates
175	  raise ``TypeError``, out-of-bounds coordinates raise ``ValueError``,
176	  duplicates within a frame are merged, and a ``start`` blocked at frame 0
177	  raises ``ValueError``. All checks run before the search starts.
178	
179	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
180	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
181	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
182	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
183	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
184	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
185	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
186	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
187	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
188	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
189	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
190	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
191	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
192	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
193	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
194	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
195	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
196	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
197	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
198	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
199	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
200	  other arrival times still compete.
201	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
202	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
203	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
204	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
205	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
206	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
207	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
208	  better route with a worse one.
209	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
210	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
211	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
212	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
213	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
214	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
215	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
216	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
217	  and step count.
218	
219	Top-k planning (``plan_k``):
220	- ``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
221	  dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None)`` returns
222	  several distinct feasible routes on the same grid in one call. It
223	  first performs exactly ``plan``'s shared validation for the
224	  dimensions, coordinates, static obstacles, positive integer cost
225	  matrix and dynamic frames (including the frame-0 start check), and
226	  only then checks ``k``: a non-bool positive integer is required,
227	  wrong types raise ``TypeError`` and non-positive values raise
228	  ``ValueError``. The optional ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost``
229	  limits are checked after all of that (the ``k`` check included),
230	  still before the search starts, with the same non-negative,
231	  non-bool integer rules ``plan`` uses (other types raise
232	  ``TypeError``, negative values raise ``ValueError``). Every error is
233	  decided before the search starts, and ``plan_k`` accepts no
234	  ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` argument.
235	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, the zero start cost, the
236	  entering-cell cost accumulation, the persistent last frame, the ban on
237	  waiting in place and on repeated coordinates, and the static/frame
238	  feasibility rules. Routes that reach the same cell through different
239	  coordinate histories are distinct candidates and are never merged, in
240	  both static and dynamic mode, so different complete coordinate
241	  sequences always remain separate results.
242	- It returns ``{"paths": [...], "costs": [...], "expanded": int}``: at
243	  most ``k`` unique complete routes ordered by ascending total cost and,
244	  on ties, by the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate
245	  sequence; ``costs`` corresponds to ``paths`` entry by entry. The first
246	  entry is the route ``plan`` would return. When no route is feasible
247	  both lists are empty and ``expanded`` still reports the route
248	  candidates actually closed to determine the answer: one count per
249	  complete history, and never counting a candidate filtered at
250	  generation or left pending. The traversal stops the moment the k-th
251	  goal route has been closed, so a small k closes strictly fewer
252	  candidates than a larger one. ``start == goal`` yields only the
253	  single-point zero-cost route, with one expansion. Every returned route
254	  verifies offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count, in
255	  both static and dynamic mode; the result never depends on obstacle-set
256	  iteration order, in-frame coordinate order or the traversal order.
257	- ``max_cost`` caps a route's accumulated entering-cell cost exactly as
258	  in ``plan``: the start still costs 0, a candidate exactly at the
259	  limit still competes and a candidate whose accumulated cost would
260	  exceed it is discarded the moment it is generated. It never changes
261	  the tie-break between legal routes. ``max_expanded`` caps the number
262	  of complete route candidates actually closed (exactly what
263	  ``expanded`` counts); once the limit is reached no further candidate
264	  is closed, and the limit only ever truncates the traversal -- it can
265	  never replace an already determined higher-ranked route. When either
266	  limit is provided the result additionally carries ``status``:
267	  ``"found"`` when all ``k`` routes were closed or the search exhausted
268	  naturally with at least one route; ``"budget_exhausted"`` when fewer
269	  than ``k`` routes were found and the budget stopped the search while
270	  candidates were still pending (this wins when both limits fire);
271	  ``"cost_exhausted"`` when fewer than ``k`` routes were found, no
272	  budget stop occurred and at least one candidate was discarded for the
273	  cost limit; ``"unreachable"`` when no route exists with neither a
274	  budget stop nor a cost discard. The routes already closed (and their
275	  costs, in rank order) are still returned when a limit ends the search
276	  early, as empty lists when none were found, and ``expanded`` is the
277	  actual closed count. Omitting both limits keeps every legacy key and
278	  value exactly unchanged.
279	
280	Batch planning (``plan_batch``):
281	- ``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None,
282	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
283	  max_cost=None)`` answers several independent single-goal queries on
284	  one shared grid in a single call. It returns ``{"results": [...]}``
285	  with exactly the result ``plan`` would return for each query, in the
286	  order of ``requests``; duplicate requests are kept and each gets its
287	  own result.
288	- The shared arguments are validated with ``plan``'s rules and order,
289	  with ``requests`` taking the position of ``start``/``goal`` in that
290	  sequence. ``requests`` must be a non-empty sequence: ``None``,
291	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
292	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each element must be a
293	  two-element sequence ``[start, goal]`` of grid coordinates: element
294	  shape or coordinate type failures raise ``TypeError``; out-of-bounds
295	  coordinates, endpoints on static obstacles and a start blocked at
296	  dynamic frame 0 raise ``ValueError``. Every check is decided before
297	  any search starts, so an invalid batch never returns partial results.
298	- Each query is an independent ``plan`` search over the shared grid:
299	  ``path``, ``cost`` and ``expanded`` are produced per request, and the
300	  ``max_expanded`` budget and the ``max_cost`` limit apply per query
301	  with no state shared across queries. ``trace``, ``status``,
302	  ``expanded_nodes``, ``checkpoint``, dynamic frames, ``start == goal``,
303	  unreachable and ``cost_exhausted`` results all follow ``plan``
304	  exactly, and a returned ``checkpoint`` can be handed to ``resume``
305	  directly. A successful path ends at its request's goal and verifies
306	  offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count. The result
307	  never depends on obstacle-set iteration order, in-frame coordinate
308	  order or the permutation of ``requests``.
309	
310	Multi-start planning (``plan_multi_start``):
311	- ``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
312	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
313	  max_cost=None)`` plans from several candidate starts to one shared
314	  goal in a single call and returns one deterministic route, in exactly
315	  the result structure of ``plan``; the path begins at the winning start
316	  and ends at ``goal``. ``starts`` takes ``start``'s position in
317	  ``plan``'s validation sequence and every shared check keeps its order,
318	  exception type and message boundary.
319	- ``starts`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates: ``None``,
320	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
321	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each start follows the
322	  coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or coordinate types
323	  raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and starts on static
324	  obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated starts merge and the tuple is
325	  sorted, so the input ordering never changes any result. A start
326	  blocked by dynamic frame 0 raises ``ValueError``; every check runs
327	  before the search starts.
328	- In static mode every start is a ``g == 0`` root and each coordinate is
329	  closed at most once: a cell keeps only its best known ``(cost, path)``
330	  pair (smallest accumulated entering-cell cost, then the
331	  lexicographically smallest complete coordinate sequence -- an ordering
332	  preserved under common extensions, so a dominated candidate can never
333	  win later). In dynamic mode the persistent last frame, the ban on
334	  waiting and on repeated coordinates apply, and routes reaching the
335	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
336	  states that are never merged.
337	- The winning route has the smallest total ``cost``; ties are decided by
338	  the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate path, so the result
339	  never depends on the input order of ``starts``. Expansion order is f,
340	  then h, then ``(x, y)`` (plus ``t`` in dynamic mode), and finally the
341	  complete path. ``cost`` counts only the cells entered (the winning
342	  start costs 0); ``expanded`` counts only closed candidates; when no
343	  route exists ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``.
344	- With ``trace=True`` static mode records the unique coordinate closing
345	  sequence and dynamic mode the ``(x, y, t)`` closing sequence, and
346	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. A ``starts`` entry equal to
347	  ``goal`` yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same
348	  start-equals-goal and zero-budget rules as ``plan``.
349	- ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost`` follow ``plan``'s ``status`` and
350	  budget-priority rules: a candidate whose accumulated cost would
351	  exceed ``max_cost`` is discarded without counting toward ``expanded``,
352	  and neither limit ever changes the unlimited route or the tie-breaks.
353	  With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop returns a JSON-serializable
354	  checkpoint recording the sorted starts, the grid constraints, the
355	  dynamic frames, the cost limit when one was provided and the complete
356	  pending state; ``resume`` continues it with the cumulative-budget,
357	  no-double-counting and only-budget-exhausted-snapshots rules of the
358	  other planners, and invalid checkpoints follow ``resume``'s usual
359	  ``TypeError``/``ValueError`` boundaries.
360	
361	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
362	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
363	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
364	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
365	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
366	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
367	  included) and before the search starts.
368	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
369	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
370	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
371	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
372	  carry the field.
373	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
374	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
375	  candidate goals, costs, dynamic frames and the cost limit when one was
376	  provided), the closed-node count, the
377	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
378	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
379	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
380	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
381	  back to ``resume`` later.
382	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
383	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
384	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
385	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
386	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
387	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
388	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
389	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
390	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
391	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
392	  closed node twice.
393	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
394	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
395	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
396	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
397	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
398	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
399	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
400	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
401	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
402	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
403	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
404	
405	Offline replay (``replay``):
406	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
407	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
408	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
409	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
410	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
411	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
412	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
413	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
414	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
415	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
416	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
417	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
418	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
419	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
420	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
421	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
422	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
423	  ``start == goal``.
424	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
425	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
426	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
427	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
428	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
429	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
430	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
431	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
432	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
433	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
434	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
435	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
436	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
437	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
438	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
439	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
440	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
441	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
442	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
443	  ever returned.
444	
445	Distance field (``distance_field``):
446	- ``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None,
447	  trace=False)`` is an offline analysis entry point for the static grid:
448	  it accepts only the dimensions, the static obstacles, a single goal and
449	  optionally ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no
450	  search budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option. The dimensions,
451	  goal coordinate, obstacle and costs checks (structure, integer types,
452	  bounds, duplicate merging, goal-on-obstacle) follow ``plan``'s public
453	  rules and order for those shared arguments and all run before the
454	  search starts; ``trace`` must be a bool (``TypeError`` otherwise).
455	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "expanded": int}`` where ``distances``
456	  is a height-by-width matrix indexed ``distances[y][x]``: ``None`` for
457	  obstacles and for cells that cannot reach the goal, ``0`` for the goal
458	  itself, and for every other reachable cell the minimum sum of the
459	  entering-cell costs along a four-neighborhood route from that cell to
460	  the goal (unit steps without ``costs``; with ``costs`` each move adds
461	  the cost of the cell entered, exactly as ``plan`` accumulates ``cost``,
462	  so a reachable ``plan`` start yields the same value ``plan`` reports
463	  as ``cost``). No reachable distance is ever negative and the matrix
464	  always matches the grid dimensions; the result is JSON-serializable.
465	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the reachable cells determined and closed
466	  once each, the goal included. The closing order is fully specified:
467	  smallest current distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate in
468	  lexicographic order, so neither the obstacle-set iteration order nor
469	  the costs layout traversal influences the matrix, the count or the
470	  trace. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally carries
471	  ``expanded_nodes``, the coordinate pairs in that closing order, and
472	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``; the field is omitted entirely
473	  when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
474	
475	Multi-goal distance field (``distance_field_any``):
476	- ``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
477	  trace=False)`` is the multi-goal counterpart of ``distance_field``:
478	  one offline analysis returns the minimum-cost field to any of the
479	  candidate endpoints in a single pass. It accepts only the dimensions,
480	  the static obstacles, a non-empty ``goals`` sequence and optionally
481	  ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no search
482	  budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option, and it never produces a
483	  ``status`` field. The dimensions, obstacles, costs and trace checks
484	  follow ``distance_field``'s public rules and order, and ``goals`` is
485	  validated exactly like ``plan_any``'s: ``None``, strings, bytes and
486	  other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, an empty sequence raises
487	  ``ValueError``, elements that are not exactly two non-bool integers
488	  raise ``TypeError``, and out-of-bounds coordinates or endpoints on
489	  static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. The goals checks occupy
490	  ``goal``'s position in ``distance_field``'s validation sequence,
491	  duplicates merge, and every check runs before the search starts, so
492	  the input permutation never changes any result.
493	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "targets": ..., "expanded": int}``.
494	  ``distances`` is the same height-by-width matrix as
495	  ``distance_field``: ``None`` for obstacles and for cells that cannot
496	  reach any endpoint, ``0`` for every endpoint, and otherwise the
497	  minimum over the endpoints of the accumulated entering-cell cost
498	  along a four-neighborhood route (unit steps without ``costs``; with
499	  ``costs`` each move adds the cost of the cell entered, the start
500	  cell's own cost never counted, exactly as ``plan``/``plan_any`` and
501	  ``distance_field`` accumulate). A reachable ``plan_any`` start yields
502	  the same value ``plan_any`` reports as ``cost``.
503	- ``targets`` is a matrix of the same shape: a reachable cell records
504	  the coordinate tuple of the endpoint that wins it, every other
505	  position is ``None`` (obstacles and unreachable cells, exactly where
506	  ``distances`` is ``None``); endpoints record themselves. When several
507	  endpoints tie at the same minimum distance the winner is the endpoint
508	  with the lexicographically smallest ``(x, y)`` coordinate, so the
509	  choice never depends on goal order. The whole result is
510	  JSON-serializable.
511	- ``expanded`` counts every reachable cell closed for the first time,
512	  all endpoints included, exactly once each. The closing order is
513	  smallest distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate
514	  lexicographically. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally
515	  carries ``expanded_nodes`` -- the coordinate pairs in that order,
516	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)`` -- and the key is omitted
517	  entirely when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
518	
519	Validation (all performed before the search starts):
520	- ``width``/``height`` must be positive integers.
521	- ``start``, ``goal`` and every entry of ``blocked`` must be grid
522	  coordinates: sequences of exactly two integers (tuples, lists, etc.),
523	  normalized to tuples.
524	- ``goals`` (``plan_any`` and ``distance_field_any``) must be a
525	  non-empty sequence of grid coordinates following the same rules,
526	  normalized, deduplicated and order-independent.
527	- ``requests`` (``plan_batch``) must be a non-empty sequence of
528	  two-element ``[start, goal]`` coordinate pairs following the same
529	  coordinate rules, with the input order and duplicates preserved.
530	- ``costs`` may be omitted or ``None`` (unit costs). Otherwise it must be a
531	  sequence of ``height`` rows, each a sequence of ``width`` positive
532	  integers; strings/bytes, non-integer cells and booleans are rejected.
533	- ``trace`` must be a bool; non-bool values raise ``TypeError``.
534	- Type or structure violations raise ``TypeError``; non-positive
535	  dimensions, out-of-bounds coordinates, endpoints on obstacles, wrong
536	  matrix shape, or non-positive cell costs raise ``ValueError``.
537	- Duplicate blocked cells are merged without changing the result.

569	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, Sequence):

592	def _normalize_blocked(blocked, width, height):
593	    if isinstance(blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(blocked, Iterable):
594	        raise TypeError(
595	            f"blocked must be an iterable of grid coordinates, "
596	            f"got {type(blocked).__name__}"
597	        )
598	    cells = set()
599	    for index, item in enumerate(blocked):
600	        name = f"blocked[{index}]"
601	        point = _normalize_point(item, name)
602	        _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
603	        cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell

607	def _normalize_costs(costs, width, height):
608	    if costs is None:
609	        return None  # unit step cost
610	    if isinstance(costs, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(costs, Sequence):
611	        raise TypeError(
612	            f"costs must be a height-by-width matrix of positive integers, "
613	            f"got {type(costs).__name__}"
614	        )
615	    if len(costs) != height:
616	        raise ValueError(
617	            f"costs must have exactly {height} rows, got {len(costs)}"
618	        )
619	    rows = []
620	    for y, row in enumerate(costs):
621	        if isinstance(row, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(row, Sequence):
622	            raise TypeError(
623	                f"costs[{y}] must be a sequence of {width} positive "
624	                f"integers, got {type(row).__name__}"
625	            )
626	        if len(row) != width:
627	            raise ValueError(
628	                f"costs[{y}] must have exactly {width} cells, "
629	                f"got {len(row)}"
630	            )
631	        parsed = []
632	        for x, cell in enumerate(row):
633	            if not _is_int(cell):
634	                raise TypeError(
635	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be an int, "
636	                    f"got {type(cell).__name__}"
637	                )
638	            if cell <= 0:
639	                raise ValueError(
640	                    f"costs[{y}][{x}] must be a positive integer, "
641	                    f"got {cell}"
642	                )
643	            parsed.append(cell)
644	        rows.append(tuple(parsed))
645	    return tuple(rows)

648	def _normalize_dynamic_blocked(dynamic_blocked, width, height):
649	    if dynamic_blocked is None:
650	        return None  # dynamic mode disabled
651	    if isinstance(dynamic_blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(
652	        dynamic_blocked, Sequence
653	    ):
654	        raise TypeError(
655	            f"dynamic_blocked must be a sequence of frames, "
656	            f"got {type(dynamic_blocked).__name__}"
657	        )
658	    if len(dynamic_blocked) == 0:
659	        return None  # no frames: equivalent to not provided
660	    frames = []
661	    for t, frame in enumerate(dynamic_blocked):
662	        if isinstance(frame, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(frame, Iterable):
663	            raise TypeError(
664	                f"dynamic_blocked[{t}] must be an iterable of grid "
665	                f"coordinates, got {type(frame).__name__}"
666	            )
667	        cells = set()
668	        for index, item in enumerate(frame):
669	            name = f"dynamic_blocked[{t}][{index}]"
670	            point = _normalize_point(item, name)
671	            _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
672	            cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
673	        frames.append(frozenset(cells))
674	    return frames

695	def _normalize_goals(goals):
696	    # ``goals`` is the plan_any counterpart of ``plan``'s single ``goal``.
697	    # This performs the outer/structure pass in exactly the position where
698	    # ``plan`` structurally normalizes ``goal``: strings, bytes, ``None``
699	    # and other non-sequences are ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence is a
700	    # ``ValueError``; every element is normalized to a coordinate tuple
701	    # (element shape/coordinate type failures are ``TypeError``). Bounds and
702	    # obstacle checks follow in ``plan_any`` at the same relative positions
703	    # ``plan`` uses for its single goal. Duplicates merge and the tuple is
704	    # sorted so the input order never affects the result.
705	    if (goals is None or isinstance(goals, (str, bytes))
706	            or not isinstance(goals, Sequence)):
707	        raise TypeError(
708	            f"goals must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates, "
709	            f"got {type(goals).__name__}"
710	        )
711	    if len(goals) == 0:
712	        raise ValueError("goals must contain at least one candidate endpoint")
713	    points = set()
714	    for index, item in enumerate(goals):
715	        point = _normalize_point(item, f"goals[{index}]")
716	        points.add(point)
717	    return tuple(sorted(points))

751	    # ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence is a ``ValueError``. Every
752	    # element must be a [start, goal] pair of grid coordinates (element

757	    # independent result.

761	            f"requests must be a non-empty sequence of [start, goal] "
762	            f"coordinate pairs, got {type(requests).__name__}"
763	        )
764	    if len(requests) == 0:
765	        raise ValueError("requests must contain at least one query")
766	    pairs = []
767	    for index, item in enumerate(requests):
768	        name = f"requests[{index}]"
769	        if isinstance(item, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(item, Sequence):
770	            raise TypeError(
771	                f"{name} must be a [start, goal] pair of grid "
772	                f"coordinates, got {type(item).__name__}"
773	            )

777	                f"got {len(item)}"
778	            )
779	        start = _normalize_point(item[0], f"{name} start")
780	        goal = _normalize_point(item[1], f"{name} goal")
781	        pairs.append((start, goal))
